title: Exact right adjoints preserve augmented derived tower completion units
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] which are Grothendieck (they admit all small colimits, filtered colimits are exact, and they have a generator), with unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], countable inverse limits, and K-injective resolutions also in their categories of strict towers [def-pur-kinjective-complex, def-weil-inverse-system]. Let $E:\mathcal A\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:U$ be an adjunction of additive exact functors. Write $U^{\mathcal T}$ for levelwise $U$, $L_{\mathcal A},L_{\mathcal B}$ for ordinary tower limits, and $RL_{\mathcal A},RL_{\mathcal B}$ for their total right derived functors [def-weil-derived-limit]. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$\gamma_X:D(U)RL_{\mathcal B}X\xrightarrow{\sim}RL_{\mathcal A}D(U^{\mathcal T})X,$$
normalized, on every strict tower complex, by the ordinary compatible-family limit isomorphism and the universal right-derived comparisons.
In addition, let $T_{\mathcal A},T_{\mathcal B}$ be additive functors from cochain complexes to cochain complexes of strict towers, respecting homotopies, with augmentations $\eta_{\mathcal A}:\Delta_{\mathcal A}\to T_{\mathcal A}$ and $\eta_{\mathcal B}:\Delta_{\mathcal B}\to T_{\mathcal B}$. Suppose they have universal total left derived presentations $LT_{\mathcal A},LT_{\mathcal B}$ with counits $\epsilon$, computed isomorphically on resolving classes $\mathcal P_{\mathcal A},\mathcal P_{\mathcal B}$: every complex receives a quasi-isomorphism from that class and each counit is invertible there. Assume $U$ sends $\mathcal P_{\mathcal B}$ into $\mathcal P_{\mathcal A}$ and an ordinary natural isomorphism
$$\theta:U^{\mathcal T}T_{\mathcal B}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{\mathcal A}U$$
commutes with the augmentations (using $U^{\mathcal T}\Delta_{\mathcal B}=\Delta_{\mathcal A}U$). There is a unique derived isomorphism $\rho:D(U^{\mathcal T})LT_{\mathcal B}\cong LT_{\mathcal A}D(U)$ satisfying the counit equation induced by $\theta$ on the resolving class. Let $c_{\mathcal A}:1\to RL_{\mathcal A}LT_{\mathcal A}$ and $c_{\mathcal B}:1\to RL_{\mathcal B}LT_{\mathcal B}$ be the normalized maps $c=RF(t)\circ v$ of [lem-weil-pbc-augmented-derived-tower-unit], taken with $G=\Delta$, $F=L$, $\nu$ the ordinary constant/limit unit, $\eta$ the given augmentation, $\alpha$ the exact derived comparison of $\Delta$, $\beta=\epsilon$, and $RF=RL$ with its universal right-derived comparison; no derived constant/limit adjunction is used. For every $M\in D(\mathcal B)$,
$$RL_{\mathcal A}(\rho_M)\,\gamma_{LT_{\mathcal B}M}\,D(U)(c_{\mathcal B,M})=c_{\mathcal A,D(U)M}.$$
Composition in this formula is right to left. The isomorphism $\gamma$ and this unit equation are independent of resolutions; no exactness of countable products is assumed.

proof.text: Upgrade each supplied K-injective tower resolution j : X → I to a monomorphic one X → Cone(id_X) ⊕ I. The mapping cone is contractible and the projection to I is a homotopy equivalence, so the new target is K-injective and the new map is a quasi-isomorphism. On K-injectives a quasi-isomorphism is a homotopy equivalence. An additive functor preserves the latter, hence the existing K-injective derivability structure computes each supplied universal right-derived comparison and makes its component invertible on K-injectives. This is implemented by the proved private helpers monicKInjectiveResolutions, derives and unitIso, using the existing source KInjectives.localizerMorphism and Mathlib Derives.isRightDerivedFunctor_of_isIso/isIso_of_isRightDerivedFunctor APIs.

source.place: Tags 070I and 070Y; explicit contractible-summand construction, implemented using the existing K-injective derivability structure

proof.text: Apply E ⊣ U levelwise to towers. Exactness is levelwise and the right adjoint U^T preserves K-injectives. Put F = L_B^complex ⋙ Q ⋙ D(U). The unit α for RLB ⋙ D(U) is D(U)δB. The unit β for D(U^T) ⋙ RLA is the composite of the exact U factor, Q(ordinaryLimitIso a), δA on U^T(X), and RLA of the inverse U^T factor. Both are invertible on K-injectives, so the derivability criterion gives two right-derived presentations of F. rightDerivedUnique gives γ with α_X γ_QX = β_X on every complex. Left-Kan injectivity gives uniqueness of γ.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); applied to the strict tower categories

proof.text: Localize the actual exact tower adjunction with its standard exact-functor factors. The private helper derivedAdjunction writes this localization for independent source/target universes (the recorded concrete helper fixes common universes). Postcomposition with the resulting right adjoint preserves the right Kan presentation of LTB: transpose a map qH → F R, lift its transpose through LTB, and transpose back. Counit naturality proves the mate equation, which proves factorization and uniqueness. The private helper kanRightAdjoint implements this full argument.

source.place: Tag 015F, exact localization; elementary natural-transformation adjunction and universal Kan calculation

proof.text:
Apply Step 3 to the natural transformation
$$LT_{\mathcal A}D(U)q_{\mathcal B}\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{\mathcal A,U(-)}}q_{\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)}T_{\mathcal A}U\xrightarrow{q(\theta^{-1})}Rq_{\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal B)}T_{\mathcal B}.$$
It gives $\sigma:LT_{\mathcal A}D(U)\to RLT_{\mathcal B}$ with
$$R(\epsilon_{\mathcal B,P})\sigma_{qP}=q(\theta_P^{-1})\epsilon_{\mathcal A,UP}.$$
For $P\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal B}$ both counits are invertible: the second because $UP\in\mathcal P_{\mathcal A}$. Hence $\sigma_{qP}$ is invertible. Every complex receives a quasi-isomorphism from such a $P$, so naturality transports this invertibility to every derived object. Define $\rho=\sigma^{-1}$. Its counit equation holds on every complex:
$$\epsilon_{\mathcal A,UP}\rho_{qP}=q(\theta_P)R(\epsilon_{\mathcal B,P}). \tag{**}$$
Uniqueness even if normalization is specified only on the resolving class follows by inverting the two counits there and transporting along each $qP\cong qM$. Thus no fullness or closure assumption on that class is being inserted. In Lean, the private natTransExtResolving helper extends equality from PB to all qX using naturality and cancellation of the image of a resolving quasi-isomorphism, then applies Localization.natTrans_ext.

source.place: Universal total left-derived counit, explicit right Kan lift and resolving-class test; agent argument

proof.text: For the supplied t and v satisfying NormalizedUnit, combine their defining equations and naturality of δ at η to prove c(QP) RL(ε_P) = Q(ν_P L(η_P)) δ_TP, with c = v ≫ RL(t). This is exactly the ordinary-map normalization of the augmented-derived-unit lemma; no existence choice is needed. The private normalizedCompletion proves it directly. The ordinary compatible-family comparison preserves ν: in each degree both composites have identity projection at every index. Naturality of the ordinary comparison and the augmentation square hη therefore identify its images of ν_B L_B(ηB) and ν_A L_A(ηA). These calculations are the private ordinaryUnitCompatibility and ordinaryCompletionCompatibility helpers.

source.place: Tag 099M, lemma-naive-completion; defining equation of the normalized constant/limit lift

proof.text: Compare the desired two natural transformations on qP for P in PB. Postcompose by RLA(LTA of the exact U factor followed by εA_UP), an isomorphism on this class. Substitute the ρ counit equation. Naturality of γ at εB_P, normalizedCompletion for B, and the all-complex γ equation replace the left side by the exact U factor followed by Q of the ordinary completion map and δA. Naturality of δA at θ_P and ordinaryCompletionCompatibility identify that ordinary map with the one for A. Naturality of cA and normalizedCompletion for A identify the right side with the same expression. Finally natTransExtResolving uses resolving quasi-isomorphisms and localization to extend equality to every derived object. This replaces the separate t/v comparison calculations of the earlier plan by a single calculation for their composite c, cancelling a counit only on the resolving class where invertibility is assumed. No exactness of countable products is used.
